body:
I don't think this is a bug.
The purpose of this option is to quickly locate the scene file associated with the node. The selected node is the context for this option. 

> "Show in FileSystem" should always highlight the "original" scene.

If you want to locate an inherited scene file, is it possible to find it quickly using a limited number of steps? It‘s "Show in FileSystem", not "Show Original in FileSystem".

Currently, it seems that finding any type of scene file can be achieved through a limited number of steps. Why would we want to limit that functionality? Besides, the rules are clear, and there are no issues that need fixing.

If you find the rules unclear, it might simply require adding some documentation.

> The purpose of this option is to quickly locate the scene file associated with the node. The selected node is the context for this option.

This does not seem like the intended purpose:

> As projects grow, it becomes very useful to be able to focus the source of an instance in your scene to manage other assets related to it in that location or do modifications to source assets.
> This commit adds that option for anything that has a source path in the Scene hierarchy, allowing easy navigation to the source of an instance. https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/84882#issue-1992679371

> They are a way to open and show the packed scene that was instancited/inherited. "Open In Editor" would do the same as the button on the right. This is possible even before saving the current scene as the one needing to be saved is the on the current inherits from. https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/119638#issuecomment-5227004819

The two comments confirm that "Show in FileSystem" should show the source of an instance, i.e. the "original" scene.

> If you want to locate an inherited scene file, is it possible to find it quickly using a limited number of steps?

Any instantiated scene file can be shown using "Open in Editor", then "Show in FileSystem" from the scene tab. Or just the latter for a normal root node. Your question seems to imply that https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/84882 has no reason to be added, which is unrelated to this issue.

> It‘s "Show in FileSystem", not "Show Original in FileSystem".

The button name is unrelated to this issue.

> Currently, it seems that finding any type of scene file can be achieved through a limited number of steps. Why would we want to limit that functionality?

Partially not true. The current scene can be shown using "Show in FileSystem" from the scene tab. The "Show in FileSystem" in normal root nodes is, at best, a duplicate. The issue is that when right-clicking the root node in an inherited scene, it shows the current scene instead of the source/ "original" scene, which makes it hard to find the source of the inherited scene. This issue limits the functionality.

> Besides, the rules are clear, and there are no issues that need fixing.

The current behaviour is not clear. For a scene instance, "Show in FileSystem" sometimes shows the source/ "original" scene, sometimes shows the current scene, and sometimes it is not available as an option.

It should have the same behaviour regardless of where the scene instance node is located in the scene tree, and whether the current scene is saved.

> If you find the rules unclear, it might simply require adding some documentation.

Documenting a bug does not make it not a bug.

As to whether this issue is a bug, let the editor/ usability teams decide.

I don't think you've grasped the priority of these rules. Since the scene's root node itself possesses multiple identities, multiple rules apply to it.

> The two comments confirm that "Show in FileSystem" should show the source of an instance, i.e. the "original" scene.

In that context, "the source of an instance" refers to the source asset. If translation leads to ambiguity, the intent of the implementation code may be clearer. 

The changes in #84882 aren't significant; why don't you take a look at the implementation?

The implementation code and the PR comments should be viewed together; looking at either one in isolation could lead to misunderstandings.

Everyone has a different knowledge background and set of habitual expressions. 

However, regarding a specific task, the intent behind a person's code and the intent behind their comments should be consistent.

I think the problem is that the option was used for two fully different thing to show in file system. This becomes really bad when both thing to show in file system happen at the same time.
I think the answer is to have options be differentiated and both options appearing on a root node of an inherited scene

I agree that "show source file" and "show current file" should be two separate options.

But does "show current file" need to appear on a root node? Considering that:
- "Show current file" is appearing on the scene tab.
  - For the current scene, the current scene tab is highlighted in the list.
  - For a different scene, the scene tab needs to be clicked before the root node can be clicked.
- Adding a new option bloats the scene tree context menu.

> "Show current file" is appearing on the scene tab. This feature itself is a way to enhance convenience. They are two different operational entry points, representing different dimensions. One approach operates from the perspective of the scene tab, while the other operates from the perspective of the scene's root node. I see no reason why they cannot coexist. It’s just like how some people are used to using a mouse, while others prefer the keyboard (although the experience in Godot is still somewhat lacking and cannot completely eliminate the need for mouse operation). > Adding a new option bloats the scene tree context menu. The `add_submenu_node_item()` method has already been provided and can be used when necessary. As shown in the image above, operations like "Copy" can also be collapsed into a submenu, just like "Create New". In the Scene Dock, operations can also be categorized by object type (such as scene roots or scripts). The current code also categorizes items, but they are not collapsed into submenus. First, implement only Pareto improvements; then, weigh non-Pareto improvements.
